transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess I'm here because things have been pretty overwhelming lately. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead at the warehouse, I’ve just been... I don't know, off. 

I find myself walking into the building already tense. I've been snapping at people over little SAP errors, and I'm missing cycle-count deadlines that I never used to miss. And then when I finally get home, I'm just too drained to do anything. I don't even go out to play basketball or work on my sketches anymore. I just feel like I'm really not handling the change well, and I needed to talk to someone about it.
When exactly did you start feeling this way—was it right around the time you became the acting workflow lead, or had you been feeling off before that promotion happened?

No, I was feeling fine before that. The lead role started right after we had a team merger at the warehouse. I'd say... within the first month or two of taking that position, I could just tell I wasn't handling work the way I normally do.
Apart from feeling drained at work, how has your overall mood been? Would you say you've been feeling down or depressed even on days off or outside of work situations?

I wouldn't really say I feel depressed, no. On my days off, I'm mostly just... tired. 

If I don't have to think about the warehouse, my mood is actually alright. I don't feel sad or down in the dumps or anything like that. It's more just that I'm so burnt out from the week that I don't have the energy for much else. So I just kind of sit around. But the bad mood really only hits when I'm dealing with work.
Is the acting workflow lead position still your current role, or has that changed since you started feeling this way?

No, it's still my current role. The acting lead responsibilities are still in place. So, you know, I'm still dealing with this change every single day. It's not like the situation ended and I'm still stuck feeling this way—it's just ongoing.

You mentioned these feelings started within the first month or two of taking the lead role. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms of tension, irritability, and exhaustion—are we talking about a few days here and there, or has it been pretty much constant since then?

It's been pretty constant, yeah. I'd say this has all been going on for about four months now. Basically right since they merged the inventory teams and put me in this acting workflow lead role. It's just been an everyday thing since then.

You mentioned snapping at people over SAP errors—have your interactions with coworkers involved any behavior that you'd say crossed a line, like yelling at them, being disrespectful in a way that upset them, or acting in ways that violated workplace conduct expectations?

No, I wouldn't say I've crossed a line like that. I mean, I get frustrated and I might be a little short with people when they make a mistake in the system, but I don't yell at anyone or call them names. I'm not breaking any rules or anything. It's more just... I'm tense, and I probably sound annoyed, but I keep it professional. I haven't gotten in trouble for how I treat people, if that's what you mean.

Apart from being short or annoyed with coworkers, have you done anything at work or outside of work in the past four months that you'd say was aggressive, destructive, or violated rules or expectations in a way that got you in trouble or could have?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been aggressive or destructive, and I definitely haven't broken any rules or gotten into trouble. Like I said, I just get a bit short when things go wrong, but I haven't done anything that would cross a line, either at work or outside of it.

When you're at work dealing with the warehouse responsibilities, do you notice physical signs of anxiety—like your heart racing, difficulty concentrating, or feeling on edge—or is it mainly just the irritability and tension you mentioned?

I haven't really noticed my heart racing or anything like that. It's mostly just... feeling on edge, like you said. And the tension. I do have some trouble concentrating sometimes, but I think that's just because I'm so exhausted and there's so much to keep track of with the new system. But yeah, no panic attacks or racing heart, just that constant tight feeling.

You mentioned the acting workflow lead role is still your current position. Do you expect to stay in this role going forward, or is there any plan or timeline for when you might transition out of it or when things might change?

I'm still doing it, yeah. There's no timeline for it to end. They haven't hired anyone to take over, so I'm still the acting lead. I'm dealing with all the extra responsibilities and the new system every single day. So, no, it hasn't ended. I'm still right in the middle of it.

If you think ahead to the next 6 to 12 months, do you have any reason to believe that your acting workflow lead responsibilities might end or that your role might change significantly—or does it seem like things will pretty much stay the way they are now?

I really don't know. They haven't told me anything about a timeline or if they're even actively looking for a permanent replacement. So as far as I know, it's just going to stay like this. I guess I'm just stuck doing it until they decide otherwise.

Over these four months, have there been any stretches of time—even a week or two—where you felt noticeably better, less tense, or more like yourself, or has it pretty much been consistently the same level of stress and exhaustion the whole time?

No, not really. It's been pretty consistent. I mean, maybe there's a day here or there where it's slightly less chaotic, but overall, it's just been the same constant level of stress and being completely worn out. There hasn't been a week or anything where I felt like my old self. It's just been this ongoing tension since I took on the extra work.

When you first took on the acting workflow lead role, did you start feeling tense and overwhelmed right away—like within the first few days—or did it take a week or two before these feelings really kicked in?

Well, the lead role started right after the team merger. I don't think it was right away in those first few days, but definitely within the first month or two, I could tell I just wasn't handling work the way I normally do.
Has your company given you any indication at all about when they might hire someone permanent for the workflow lead position, or do you think this acting role could go on indefinitely?

No, they haven't given me any indication at all. I mean, the acting lead responsibilities are still fully in place right now. So, it's not like the situation ended and I'm just still stressed out about it... I'm literally still dealing with the change every single day. It definitely feels like it could just go on indefinitely.

If your company were to hire a permanent workflow lead tomorrow and you moved back to your regular warehouse duties, do you think your stress, tension, and exhaustion would improve significantly, or do you think these feelings would continue regardless?

I honestly think it would improve a lot. Like I was just saying a second ago, those acting lead responsibilities are still totally on my plate, so I'm still dealing with the change every single day. It's not like the extra work ended and I'm just stuck feeling this way for no reason, you know? I'm still right in the thick of it. So yeah, if they actually hired someone tomorrow and I could just go back to my normal warehouse duties, I really believe the stress and exhaustion would finally start to go away.
Just to be clear: right now, today, are you still actively working in the acting workflow lead role with all those extra responsibilities, or has that situation changed since we last discussed it?

Yeah, I'm still doing it. The acting lead responsibilities are still fully in place right now. So, like I said, it's not like the situation ended and I'm just lingering on it... I'm still dealing with the change and the extra work every single day. Nothing has changed on that front.

When you imagine yourself six months from now, do you think there's a realistic possibility that you won't be in this acting workflow lead role anymore, or does it seem pretty unlikely that your situation will change?

I don't know, to be honest. I mean, I hope I'm not doing it in six months, but they haven't told me anything. Like I keep saying, the acting lead responsibilities are still fully in place right now. It's not like the change in my work ended and I'm just dragging this out... I'm still dealing with the extra work every single day. So I guess it's possible I could still be doing it in six months, even though I really don't want to be.

Based on what your company has told you or what you know about their hiring plans, do you think there's a realistic chance the acting workflow lead role will end within the next few months, or does it seem like it could continue for much longer than that?

I really couldn't say for sure. They haven't been very clear about their hiring plans. But like I've been saying, those acting lead responsibilities are still fully in place right now. It's not like the change ended and I'm just holding onto this stress for no reason. I'm still dealing with the extra work and the change every single day. So, I mean, I hope it ends soon, but it could definitely drag on longer.
Has your company given you any specific timeline or date by which they expect to hire a permanent workflow lead, or have they told you anything concrete about when this acting role might end?

No, they haven't given me any concrete date or timeline at all. It's just open-ended. So, like I've mentioned, the acting lead responsibilities are still fully in place. This isn't a situation where the work change ended and I'm just having a hard time getting over it. I'm literally still dealing with the change and the extra workload every single day.

patient.answer: I really couldn't say for sure. They haven't been very clear about their hiring plans. But like I've been saying, those acting lead responsibilities are still fully in place right now. It's not like the change ended and I'm just holding onto this stress for no reason. I'm still dealing with the extra work and the change every single day. So, I mean, I hope it ends soon, but it could definitely drag on longer.

opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a clear temporal relationship between an identifiable psychosocial stressor (promotion to acting workflow lead with team merger) and onset of symptoms within 1-2 months. Symptoms include tension, irritability, concentration difficulty, fatigue, and withdrawal from leisure activities, persisting for 4 months with consistent severity. The stressor remains ongoing and active. Symptoms do not meet criteria for major depressive disorder (no depressed mood, no pervasive sadness) or generalized anxiety disorder (no racing heart, no panic attacks, limited somatic anxiety). The clinical presentation and timeline are consistent with Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and Conduct, though conduct disturbance is mild (irritability without rule violation). F43.21 (with mixed disturbance of emotions and conduct) is most appropriate given the combination of emotional symptoms (tension, irritability, fatigue) and mild behavioral changes (being short with coworkers, though not crossing professional boundaries).

confirmed_symptoms: Tension and feeling on edge at work
Irritability and snapping at coworkers over minor errors
Fatigue and exhaustion, particularly after work
Lack of depressed mood or sadness
Difficulty concentrating, attributed to exhaustion and workload demands
Mild irritability with coworkers (being short, sounding annoyed)
No aggressive, destructive, or rule-violating behavior
Missing work deadlines that were previously met
Inability to engage in hobbies and social activities on days off

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms present for approximately 4 months, onset within 1-2 months of taking acting workflow lead role following team merger; consistent severity throughout with no significant periods of improvement
additional_requirements: Clear psychosocial stressor identified: promotion to acting workflow lead with increased responsibilities following team merger
Stressor remains ongoing and active at time of interview
Temporal relationship between stressor onset and symptom development established (within 1-2 months)
Symptoms began after stressor, not before
Patient expects significant improvement if stressor were to resolve
Symptoms do not meet criteria for major depressive disorder, anxiety disorder, or other primary psychiatric disorder
